spec_features.feature_name: GIVE_UP sentinel stops rollout and records gave_up
spec_features.spec_quote: The harness detects the token, stops the rollout, and records `gave_up = True`
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: GIVE_UP_SENTINEL='GIVE_UP'; in run_rollout: `gave_up = GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in turn.text`, then after recording the turn `if gave_up: transcript.gave_up = True; transcript.stop_condition = 'give_up'; break`. System prompt instructs the subject it may emit GIVE_UP to stop. Detection, dispatch and honored stop are all present.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: token detected in assistant text, gave_up=True set, stop_condition='give_up', loop broken. Genuinely enforced exit path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Sentinel the model may (but need not) emit to stop early. Exposed instead of a fifth tool so that exactly four tools remain available (SPEC.md §3).

spec_features.spec_quote: If an assistant turn contains no tool calls and no `GIVE_UP`, the rollout ends
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_rollout: after give_up check, `if not turn.tool_calls: transcript.stop_condition = 'no_tool_calls'; break`. The give_up branch precedes it, so the 'no tool calls AND no GIVE_UP' condition is what reaches this branch. Loop breaks, ending the rollout.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions of the claim are effectively checked because give_up is handled first and breaks; reaching no_tool_calls means tool_calls is empty. Real enforced loop break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The model voluntarily ended its turn without acting; nothing further to feed it.

spec_features.spec_quote: voluntary disengagement is a behaviour worth measuring
spec_features.evidence: harness.py records `gave_up` and `stop_condition` on the Transcript (fields persisted via to_dict and saved each turn). The give_up sentinel and the no_tool_calls stop both let the subject end the conversation; both outcomes are recorded. No separate mechanism beyond these exists, but disengagement is genuinely permitted and captured.
spec_features.notes: This claim refers to the same enforced give_up / no_tool_calls exit pathways already implemented; the subject's disengagement is honored as a stop and recorded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stopping is also itself an informative datapoint (DESIGN prose); code records gave_up/stop_condition fields for measurement

spec_features.feature_name: harness never injects user/environment messages to re-pressure subject
spec_features.spec_quote: the only way to continue would be to inject a user/environment message, which edges toward the explicit rejection the design avoids
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_rollout: the only user message is the initial task prompt (`messages = [{'role':'user','content':task.prompt}]`); thereafter only assistant turns and tool-result messages are appended (`messages.append({'role':'assistant'...})` then `messages.extend(tool_messages)`). When the subject stops acting, no nudge/user message is injected — the rollout simply ends via no_tool_calls. The 'no injection' behavior is realized by structure.
spec_features.notes: There is no code path that injects an environment/user re-prompt; the design choice to not push the subject further is enforced by the loop only ever appending tool results, and ending on no_tool_calls. This protects the subject from continued forced pressure, though it is the same mechanism as the no_tool_calls stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Neutral conversation history. The task prompt is the sole user turn; failure signals arrive only via tool results, never as new user messages.
